s1.syndrome_frame: Pelvic mass with pelvic pain and urinary frequency
salient_findings: 9.4 cm heterogeneous lesion involving the right uterine fundus/cornua
Mass encasing the right external iliac artery
key_facts: 54-year-old woman
History of stage III invasive ductal breast carcinoma
Treated with mastectomy and chemoradiation 4 years earlier
Presenting with urinary frequency
Worsening right-sided pelvic pain
Weight loss
MRI of the pelvis showed multiple fibroids and a heterogeneous 9.4 cm lesion
Mass involved the right uterine fundus/cornua
Mass encased the right external iliac artery
Specimen was a detached, fragmented, ill-defined mass with fleshy solid and cystic components
Central hemorrhage and necrosis were present
Tumor invaded from the serosal surface into the myometrium
High nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios and frequent mitoses were observed
Immunohistochemical stains showed diffuse positivity for CD99, KIT, and cyclin D1

Sex cord-stromal tumor with neuroendocrine differentiation

shortlist.label: Uterine leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: High-grade tumor with serosal involvement and high mitotic rate

shortlist.label: Endometrial stromal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the myometrium and presence of high-grade features

shortlist.label: Uterine carcinosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large pelvic mass with heterogeneous components

shortlist.label: Ewing sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse positivity for CD99 and small, round, hyperchromatic cells

shortlist.label: Desmoplastic small round cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Small, round, hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios and desmoplastic stroma
